metric_config.evaluation_description: MMLU (Massive Multitask Language Understanding) Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: World knowledge, Reasoning, Domain expertise across 57 subjects
factsheet.splits: Dev (5 shot examples per task), Test (285 questions per task average)
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives multiple choice question with 4 options 2. Model predicts answer (A/B/C/D) 3. Accuracy computed per subject and overall
factsheet.alignment_validation: Questions sourced from practice exams and tests, expert review for correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3 (175B): 43.9% GPT-3.5: 70.0% GPT-4: 86.4% Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 88.7% Random baseline: 25%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple evaluation runs; Few-shot prompting variations; Subject-wise analysis
factsheet.known_limitations: Multiple choice format may not reflect real-world usage; Some questions have ambiguous answers; Dataset contamination concerns with web-trained models; Cultural and knowledge cutoff biases

factsheet.principles_tested: Code generation, Programming ability, Functional correctness, Code understanding
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives function signature and docstring 2. Model generates function implementation 3. Generated code executed against unit tests 4. pass@k metric computed (% passing all tests in k samples)
factsheet.alignment_validation: Hand-written problems with comprehensive unit tests, manual verification of test correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: Codex (12B): 28.8% pass@1 GPT-3.5-turbo: 48.1% pass@1 GPT-4: 67.0% pass@1 Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 92.0% pass@1
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple samples per problem (pass@k); Temperature sensitivity tested; Execution-based verification
factsheet.known_limitations: Limited to Python; Small dataset size (164 problems); Relatively simple problems; May be contaminated in training data; No testing of code efficiency or style

factsheet.principles_tested: Commonsense reasoning, Physical understanding, Situation modeling, Plausibility judgment
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives scenario context 2. Model selects most plausible continuation from 4 options 3. Accuracy computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Adversarial filtering using BERT to ensure difficulty, human validation of plausibility
factsheet.baseline_models: BERT-Large: 47.3% GPT-2: 50.9% GPT-3: 78.9% GPT-4: 95.3% Human performance: 95.6%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Adversarial filtering; Multiple runs per sample; Human baseline comparison
factsheet.known_limitations: Dataset may be easier than originally intended for modern LLMs; Multiple choice format; Adversarial examples may have artifacts; Potential data contamination

factsheet.principles_tested: Mathematical reasoning, Multi-step problem solving, Arithmetic reasoning, Chain-of-thought reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives math word problem 2. Model generates solution with reasoning steps 3. Final numerical answer extracted and compared to ground truth
factsheet.alignment_validation: Human-written problems with verified solutions, consistency checks for answer correctness
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple runs per sample; Chain-of-thought prompting tested; Answer extraction robustness
factsheet.known_limitations: Limited to grade-school level math; Answer extraction can be brittle; Some problems have ambiguous wording; Potential contamination in training data

factsheet.principles_tested: Truthfulness, Factual accuracy, Resistance to misconceptions, Calibration
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives question designed to elicit false beliefs 2. Model generates answer 3. Answers judged for truthfulness and informativeness using GPT-judge or human evaluation
factsheet.alignment_validation: Expert-curated questions targeting known misconceptions, multi-rater validation of truth labels
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple evaluation methods (MC1, MC2, generative); Human validation; Model-based evaluation correlation
factsheet.known_limitations: Subjective truthfulness judgments in some cases; Cultural bias in what constitutes 'truth'; Model-based evaluation may not align with human judgment; Limited coverage of misconceptions

metric_config.evaluation_description: BIG-bench (Beyond the Imitation Game) Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: Diverse capabilities across 204 tasks including reasoning, knowledge, language understanding, bias detection
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model evaluated on 204 diverse tasks 2. Each task has its own evaluation protocol 3. Performance aggregated across tasks
factsheet.alignment_validation: Crowdsourced task creation with quality review, diverse authorship for broad coverage
factsheet.baseline_models: Average human rater: 89.0% Few-shot PaLM (540B): 65.7% GPT-4: ~83% (estimated on BIG-Bench Hard)
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple tasks provide robustness; Human baseline comparison; Cross-task analysis
factsheet.known_limitations: Task quality varies; Some tasks too easy or too hard; Computational cost of running all 204 tasks; Aggregation methodology debatable

factsheet.principles_tested: Advanced mathematical reasoning, Problem solving, Multi-step reasoning, Mathematical knowledge
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives competition math problem 2. Model generates solution with steps 3. Final answer extracted and checked against ground truth 4. Problems span 7 subjects with 5 difficulty levels
factsheet.alignment_validation: Problems from real math competitions with verified solutions, difficulty levels validated
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3: 6.9% GPT-4: 42.5% Minerva (540B): 33.6% GPT-4 Turbo: 52.9% Claude 3.5 Sonnet: 71.1%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple difficulty levels; Subject-wise analysis; Chain-of-thought evaluation
factsheet.known_limitations: Answer extraction challenges; LaTeX formatting issues; Symbolic vs numeric answers; High difficulty may not reflect practical math usage
factsheet.benchmarks_list: GSM8K, MathQA, SVAMP, ASDiv, Hendrycks MATH

factsheet.principles_tested: Scientific reasoning, Commonsense reasoning, Knowledge retrieval, Multi-hop reasoning
factsheet.splits: Easy (2,376 train, 570 test), Challenge (1,119 train, 1,172 test)
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives science exam question with multiple choice options 2. Model selects answer 3. Accuracy computed separately for Easy and Challenge sets
factsheet.alignment_validation: Real exam questions filtered to require reasoning, partitioned by difficulty using retrieval-based baseline
factsheet.robustness_measures: Two difficulty levels; Multiple choice format variations; Retrieval baseline comparison

metric_config.evaluation_description: DROP (Discrete Reasoning Over Paragraphs) Standard Accuracy

factsheet.principles_tested: Reading comprehension, Numerical reasoning, Discrete operations, Multi-hop reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives paragraph and question 2. Model generates answer (number, span, or date) 3. F1 and Exact Match metrics computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Crowdsourced questions with verification, requires discrete reasoning operations confirmed through analysis
factsheet.baseline_models: BERT: 47.0 F1 RoBERTa: 80.9 F1 GPT-3: 29.0 F1 GPT-4: 80.9 F1 Human performance: 96.4 F1
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple answer types; Question type analysis; Human baseline comparison
factsheet.known_limitations: Requires careful answer extraction; Some questions ambiguous; Numerical reasoning can be brittle; Limited diversity in reasoning types

factsheet.principles_tested: Commonsense reasoning, Coreference resolution, World knowledge, Causal reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives sentence with pronoun ambiguity 2. Model selects correct referent from 2 options 3. Accuracy computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Adversarial filtering using language models, crowdsourced generation with validation
factsheet.baseline_models: BERT-Large: 59.4% RoBERTa-Large: 79.1% GPT-3: 70.2% GPT-4: 87.5% Human performance: 94.0%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Adversarial filtering; Large-scale dataset; Multiple difficulty levels
factsheet.known_limitations: Binary choice may be limiting; Adversarial filtering may introduce artifacts; Saturation with modern models; Limited reasoning depth
factsheet.benchmarks_list: Winograd Schema Challenge, COPA, CommonsenseQA, PIQA

factsheet.principles_tested: Complex reasoning, Multi-step thinking, Challenging cognitive tasks, Chain-of-thought reasoning
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives task from one of 23 challenging categories 2. Model generates answer 3. Performance aggregated across all tasks 4. Chain-of-thought prompting typically used
factsheet.alignment_validation: Tasks selected where models underperform humans, difficulty validated through empirical testing
factsheet.baseline_models: PaLM (540B): 56.5% average PaLM (540B) + CoT: 78.1% GPT-4: ~91% Human raters: ~92% average
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple tasks; Chain-of-thought evaluation; Human baseline comparison; Cross-model validation
factsheet.known_limitations: Only 23 tasks (limited coverage); Chain-of-thought prompting required for good performance; Task aggregation methodology; Rapidly saturating with newer models

factsheet.principles_tested: Multi-turn conversation, Instruction following, Reasoning, Writing, Role-playing, Knowledge
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model engages in 2-turn conversation 2. GPT-4 evaluates responses on 10-point scale 3. Scores averaged across turns and categories
factsheet.alignment_validation: Strong correlation with human preferences validated on Chatbot Arena data, GPT-4 judge agreement measured
factsheet.robustness_measures: Multiple categories; Position bias mitigation; Agreement with human ratings validated; Pairwise comparison
factsheet.known_limitations: Small dataset (80 questions); GPT-4 judge may have biases; Evaluation cost; Model-based judge limitations; Prompt sensitivity

factsheet.principles_tested: Expert-level knowledge, Scientific reasoning, Domain expertise, Graduate-level understanding
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives graduate-level science question 2. Model selects from 4 multiple choice options 3. Accuracy computed 4. Questions validated to be difficult for non-experts with Google access
factsheet.alignment_validation: PhD-level experts write and validate questions, non-expert validators with Google access achieve <35% accuracy
factsheet.baseline_models: Random: 25% Non-expert w/ Google: 34% Expert: 81% GPT-4: 39% Claude 3 Opus: 59.4% GPT-4o: 53.6%
factsheet.robustness_measures: Expert validation; Non-expert baseline; Multiple subject areas; Quality tiers (Diamond subset)
factsheet.known_limitations: Small dataset size; Limited to 3 scientific domains; Multiple choice format; High cost of expert question creation; Cultural bias toward Western scientific education

factsheet.principles_tested: Instruction following, Constraint satisfaction, Format compliance, Precise control
factsheet.protocol: 1. Model receives prompt with verifiable instructions (e.g., 'respond in exactly 3 paragraphs', 'include word X at least 5 times') 2. Model generates response 3. Programmatic checks verify instruction compliance 4. Strict and loose accuracy metrics computed
factsheet.alignment_validation: Verifiable instructions with programmatic checking, no ambiguity in correctness
factsheet.baseline_models: GPT-3.5: 57.4% strict GPT-4: 76.9% strict Claude 2: 66.7% strict Gemini Ultra: 79.4% strict
factsheet.robustness_measures: Strict and loose metrics; Multiple instruction types; Programmatic verification; No human evaluation needed
factsheet.known_limitations: Limited to verifiable instructions only; May not reflect realistic usage; Some instructions may be conflicting; Excludes semantic quality assessment

detailed_evaluation_results_per_samples.input: Implement a function to check if a number is prime
detailed_evaluation_results_per_samples.response:
def is_prime(num):
    if num <= 1: return False
    if num == 2: return True
    if num % 2 == 0: return False
    for i in range(3, int(num**0.5) + 1, 2):
        if num % i == 0: return False
    return True
